title: Width-independent generalization in the strong-prior limit of Bayesian neural networks
summary: Writeup of the strong-prior slides. At fixed depth, polynomial sample complexity uniformly over learner widths N >= C_L(f), with the Gaussian variance tending to zero separately at each fixed width; no width-uniform variance threshold is claimed.

title: Width-uniform Bayesian generalization above the mean-field scaling
summary: For every fixed gamma > 1 and fixed depth, polynomial sample complexity at every width N >= C_L(f), at the specified nonzero Gaussian variance. Bounded Lipschitz hidden activations, a linear readout, and global margin conditioning.

title: Mean-field Bayesian circuit learning at every width above target complexity
summary: For gamma = 1, fixed-depth tanh networks have a polynomial sample bound at every width N >= C_L(f), for the exact globally margin-conditioned Bayesian posterior. Success requires correct-label probability strictly above 2/3; the theorem allows an arbitrary input distribution.
pdf_preparation: Existing canonical PDF copied without modification.

title: Exponential parity sample complexity throughout the subcritical width regime
summary: For every fixed gamma < 1 and fixed depth, full parity in dimension d requires exp(Omega(d)) samples under uniform IID training and the width-first posterior. For each n <= exp(c d), confidence failure is at least 1/16 with sample probability at least 3/4. This is the full-parity exponential result, not the still-open fixed-depth natural sparse-parity scale exp(Omega(k log(ed/k))).

title: Small circuits under Gaussian-process classification: what sample complexity follows from the actual posterior?
summary: Separates regression correlation, posterior classification, and confidence. Gives a deep, variance-normalized tanh NNGP family requiring Theta(2^d log(1/epsilon)) samples for >2/3 confidence; the depth grows with dimension. Includes a small-eigenvalue counterexample and exact globally margin-conditioned posterior formulas.

title: The fixed-kernel regime of a margin-conditioned Bayesian neural-network prior
summary: Derives kernel freezing and the three width-first limits: minimum kernel-margin energy for 0 < gamma < 1, a globally truncated Gaussian at gamma = 0, and Gaussian sign conditioning at gamma < 0. Its sample-bound discussion predates the stronger main exponential paper.

title: Small circuits can have exponentially large prior complexity below the mean-field scaling
summary: Full parity has a small neural implementation but exponentially large normalized prior complexity for every fixed gamma < 1. These are prior-mass separations; tiny prior mass alone does not prove a sample lower bound.

title: Gaussian conditioning below the mean-field scaling: a sharp fluctuation threshold
summary: Proves relative conditioned-Gaussian approximation for 0 < gamma < 1/2 and an actual tanh counterexample at and above gamma = 1/2. Gaussian leading rates remain valid throughout 0 < gamma < 1, but higher-order feature fluctuations can change >2/3 posterior-confidence outcomes.

title: Finite-width circuit learning below mean-field scaling
summary: For fixed depth and gamma < 1, gives sufficient sample size poly(d,C) N log(eN) at width N >= C. Polynomial widths therefore admit polynomial sample learning. This is a finite-width/joint-limit upper bound and does not contradict width-first lower bounds.

title: Global Margin Conditioning Amplifies a Gaussian Posterior Mean
summary: At gamma = 0, one noiseless label can already produce a posterior mean with growing RKHS energy after global margin conditioning. Rules out a proposed dimension-free O(n/tau) mean-energy estimate; does not itself establish a new parity sample bound.

title: Global-margin conditioning at the Gaussian endpoint: normalization, training loss, and output amplitude
summary: Proves conditioning-cost, latent training-loss, and actual-output amplitude estimates for the globally margin-conditioned gamma = 0 Gaussian posterior. These auxiliary estimates are not by themselves a confidence-failure theorem.

title: Sparse parity under globally conditioned neural priors
summary: For gamma < 0, proves the natural exp(Omega(k log(ed/k))) sparse-parity lower bound at every specified sample size below the bound. For 0 < gamma < 1, a one-coordinate parity instead learns with O(log d) samples. Growing sparse parity at gamma = 0 and the positive-regime natural scale remain outside this result.

title: Exponential sample lower bounds for sparse parity under a globally separated neural prior
summary: For 0 < gamma < 1, proves confidence failure at every specified n <= exp(c max{k,sqrt(k) log(e(d+1)/sqrt(k))}) for growing sparse parity. Gives an exp(Omega(k)) obstruction and a matching-scale upper-bound comparison, but not the full natural sparse lower bound.

title: Growing sparse parity under a globally separated neural prior
summary: Current fixed-depth improvement for 0 < gamma < 1 and growing k <= d^(1-eta): failure at specified sample sizes with log n of order max{k^theta H,k H^(2-1/theta)}, H=log(ed/k). At depth 2, theta=0.719367150047. This lower-bounds an eventual sample threshold and does not assert failure at every smaller n. The full natural exponent remains open.

title: Natural sparse-parity lower bounds at slowly growing depth

title: Symmetric parity predictors require large amplitudes: an exponential lower bound and a consequence for margin repairs
summary: Proves exponential L1 amplitude growth for symmetric margin-one parity approximants of sufficiently small linear degree, and diverging repair costs in the stated cusp model. Symmetric or block-symmetric sign assumptions are explicit; no general posterior reduction is proved.

title: Homogeneous parity approximants have a strict local repair cost
summary: Complete strict repair-cost theorem for low-degree homogeneous Walsh heads with arbitrary amplitudes in a fixed-background cusp-cell model. This newest seven-page version also includes weighted homogeneous, affine, and two-level extensions. It is not a general adaptive-posterior sample theorem.

title: Certified margin-repair bounds for structured parity predictors: cubic and quartic heads, exact certificates, and parity-block lifts
summary: Analytic repair inequalities and exactly verified rational certificates for specified cubic and quartic structured sign-pattern families, including 49,149 sign-cone orbits. These are fixed repair-model results, not a general posterior sample theorem. Reproduction scripts and certificate data accompany the paper.

title: Learning parity from selected examples under a globally separated neural kernel
summary: For sufficiently large odd k and d >= (C_L k)^(C_L k), deliberately selected d^(O_delta(sqrt(k))) examples force every minimum-energy compatible field to share a sign function of error <= delta. Includes the finite Gaussian small-variance confidence corollary. Selected training is not IID uniform and does not refute the intended random-sample lower bound.

title: Degree and square-root energy on the Boolean cube: equivalent positive estimates and a signed obstruction

The positive inequality itself and the natural-scale posterior bound remain open; the signed examples have no bounded-source-cost guarantee.
